text: AI hiring/recruitment tools (resume screening, candidate ranking, AI interview agents, performance evaluation, promotion, task allocation, termination) fall under Annex III, Section 4 as high-risk AI systems.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Annex III point 4(a): 'AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates'; 4(b) covers promotion, termination, task allocation, monitoring and evaluating performance.
notes: Annex III uses 'points', not 'sections'.

text: High-risk deployer obligations include: using the system per provider instructions, implementing human oversight, monitoring performance and reporting serious incidents, informing workers/representatives when AI affects employment decisions, and not using the system outside its intended purpose.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 26(1) use 'in accordance with the instructions for use'; 26(2) human oversight; 26(5) monitor and report serious incidents; 26(7) 'deployers who are employers shall inform workers' representatives and the affected workers'
notes: 'Not using the system outside its intended purpose' is not stated as such; it follows from 26(1) and Art 25(1)(c).

text: Providers of high-risk AI systems bear pre-market obligations under Articles 8-15: risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging/record-keeping, transparency to deployers, human oversight design, and accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 16(a): providers ensure compliance with Section 2; Section 2 = Arts 8-15 (risk management 9, data 10, documentation 11, logs 12, transparency 13, oversight 14, accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity 15).

text: Article 27 requires a Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment (FRIA) before first use, applicable to public-sector deployers, private entities providing public services, and deployers of certain Annex III systems (points 5(b) and (c)), excluding Annex III point 2 (critical infrastructure).
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 27(1) (see C026); 27(2): 'The obligation laid down in paragraph 1 applies to the first use of the high-risk AI system.'

text: Article 6(3) provides a derogation allowing an Annex III AI system to be considered non-high-risk if it does not pose significant risk of harm, e.g., performing a narrow procedural task, but this exemption is not available where the system profiles natural persons and must be documented.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 6(3): 'an AI system referred to in Annex III shall always be considered to be high-risk where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons'; 6(4): 'shall document its assessment'

text: Deployers must also fulfill Article 4 AI literacy obligations, which remain in force regardless of the Annex III compliance deadline extension.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 4(1) as amended: 'Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to support the development of AI literacy of their staff'; Chapter I applies from 2 Feb 2025.

text: The original compliance deadline for high-risk Annex III obligations, including recruitment tools, was August 2, 2026.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113 (2024 text): 'It shall apply from 2 August 2026.' ... '(c) Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations in this Regulation shall apply from 2 August 2027.'

text: Under the Digital Omnibus agreement, compliance obligations for standalone high-risk AI systems under Annex III (including recruitment/hiring tools) have been deferred to December 2, 2027.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113(c) as amended: 'Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'

text: The Digital Omnibus received final approval by the Council on June 29, 2026, replacing the original August 2, 2026 deadline.
label: correct
evidence_quote: 'Today, the Council gave its final green light on a new regulation aiming to streamline and simplify certain rules regarding artificial intelligence (AI).' (29 June 2026)

text: As of June 2026, the Digital Omnibus deferral had been approved by the European Parliament (per one source's account).
label: correct
evidence_quote: Footnote 4: 'Position of the European Parliament of 16 June 2026 (not yet published in the Official Journal) and decision of the Council of 29 June 2026.'; Art 4: enters into force on the third day following publication (OJ 24.7.2026).
notes: 'June 2026' matches the Parliament position of 16 June 2026.

text: AI embedded in regulated products (as opposed to standalone Annex III systems) will be subject to high-risk obligations from August 2, 2028.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113(c) as amended: 'Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'

text: Prohibitions on unacceptable-risk AI practices (Article 5) took effect in February 2025.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113(a): 'Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025'

text: Obligations for general-purpose AI (GPAI) models took effect/became enforceable from August 2026.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Art 113(b): 'Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101'
notes: GPAI obligations took effect 2 Aug 2025; only enforcement (Art 101 fines) from Aug 2026.

text: From August 2, 2026, the European Commission's AI Office, together with national authorities, began enforcing the AI Act, alongside new transparency requirements applying from that date.
label: correct
evidence_quote: 'From 2 August 2026, the AI Office and authorities of the Member States are responsible for implementing, supervising and enforcing the AI Act.' Art 50 applies from the general date, 2 Aug 2026.
notes: Matches the Commission's own wording.

text: National Market Surveillance Authorities, designated by each Member State, undertake most compliance investigations and enforcement actions under the AI Act, applying EU Regulation 2019/1020.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 70(1): each Member State designates 'at least one market surveillance authority'; Art 74(1): 'Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to AI systems covered by this Regulation.'
notes: 'Most' is a characterization; the AI Office covers GPAI models and some AI systems (Art 75(1)).

text: The AI Office holds enforcement powers over GPAI models specifically, including requesting technical documentation, evaluating models, requiring corrective measures, and issuing fines.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 88(1): 'The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V ... The Commission shall entrust the implementation of these tasks to the AI Office'
notes: Also Arts 91-93 and 101.

text: Penalties for non-compliance with high-risk obligations (Annex III) can reach €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 99(4): 'administrative fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 3 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher'
notes: Covers Art 16 (providers) and Art 26 (deployers).

text: Penalties for prohibited AI practices under Article 5 can reach €35 million or 7% of worldwide annual turnover.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 99(3): 'Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.'

text: Penalties for supplying incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information to authorities can reach €7.5 million or 1% of worldwide annual turnover; the same maximum applies to failure to comply with a request for information (RFI).
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Art 99(5): 'The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 7 500 000 or ... up to 1 %'
notes: First half right. No 7.5M/1% tier for failing to comply with a request: for GPAI it is Art 101(1)(b), up to 3%/EUR 15M; for AI Office decisions Art 75c(4) points to Art 99(4).

text: GPAI provider violations can be penalized up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, with Commission enforcement from August 2026.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 101(1): 'The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher'
notes: Art 101 applies from 2 Aug 2026.

text: Penalties under the AI Act could begin applying from August 2, 2025, except for GPAI obligations, which take effect August 2, 2026 (per a 2024 analysis).
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113(b): 'Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101'
notes: Read as GPAI fines (Art 101), which apply from 2 Aug 2026. GPAI obligations themselves applied from 2 Aug 2025.

text: Providers and deployers are the two primary actors bearing AI Act obligations, with importers and other actors also covered under Articles 22-25.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Arts 22 (authorised representatives), 23 (importers), 24 (distributors), 25 (value chain).
notes: 'Primary actors' is interpretation.

text: Article 53 AI Act requires GPAI model providers to maintain technical documentation, make information available to downstream providers, and put in place a policy to comply with EU copyright law, including identifying and complying with TDM opt-out reservations of rights.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 53(1)(c): 'identify and comply with ... a reservation of rights expressed pursuant to Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790'

text: Article 53 requires GPAI providers to publish a 'sufficiently detailed summary' of training data content.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 53(1)(d): 'draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training'

text: Providers of GPAI models released under free and open-source licences (allowing access, use, modification and distribution) are subject to lighter obligations under Article 53(2), exempting them from technical documentation and some transparency requirements (with exceptions for systemic risk models).
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 53(2): 'The obligations set out in paragraph 1, points (a) and (b), shall not apply to providers of AI models that are released under a free and open-source licence ... This exception shall not apply to general-purpose AI models with systemic risks.'

text: Chapter V (Articles 53, 54, 55) of the AI Act sets out specific legal obligations for GPAI model providers, with additional obligations for those posing systemic risk.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Chapter V, Section 2 (Arts 53-54) and Section 3 (Art 55, systemic risk).

text: A GPAI model is considered to present systemic risk if it has high-impact capabilities or significant impact on the Union market due to reach, per Recitals 110-111.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Recital 111: 'a general-purpose AI model should be considered to present systemic risks if it has high-impact capabilities ... or significant impact on the internal market due to its reach.'

text: The AI Office within the European Commission has exclusive competence to supervise and enforce GPAI model obligations, distinct from the decentralized national authority model used for high-risk AI systems.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 88(1): 'The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V ... The Commission shall entrust the implementation of these tasks to the AI Office'

text: Fines for GPAI-related infringements under the AI Act can reach up to 3% of global annual turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 101(1): 'The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher'

text: Article 99 penalties for prohibited-practice infringements (Article 5) can reach up to 7% of worldwide annual turnover or EUR 35 million, whichever is higher.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 99(3): 'Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.'

text: Non-compliance with the EU AI Act carries maximum fines of €35 million.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Art 99(3): 'Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of its total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher.'
notes: The maximum is EUR 35M or 7% of turnover, whichever is higher, so it can exceed EUR 35M.

text: GPAI providers must comply with obligations effective August 2, 2025; enforcement by the European Commission begins August 2, 2026; models already on the market before August 2, 2025 must comply by August 2, 2027.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113(b): 'Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025, with the exception of Article 101' Art 111(3): comply 'by 2 August 2027'.

text: The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) was adopted/dated 13 June 2024.
label: correct
evidence_quote: 'Done at Brussels, 13 June 2024.'

text: The EU AI Act was 'agreed upon' in 2024 and 'updated' in 2025.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Consolidated text lists one amendment only: 'REGULATION (EU) 2026/1744 ... of 8 July 2026'
notes: No amendment in 2025.

text: Generic GPAI models are subject to mere transparency obligations under Article 53, consisting of maintaining technical documentation understandable to the AI Office and to third parties integrating the model.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 53(1)(a) documentation for the AI Office; (b) information to downstream providers
notes: Leaves out (c) copyright policy and (d) training summary; 'consisting of' can read as a full list.

text: There is no comprehensive federal AI law in the US comparable to the EU AI Act, though there have been various federal laws and initiatives across administrations, including export controls, investment restrictions, and infrastructure funding support.
label: unverifiable
notes: Absence claim and 'comprehensive' (rule 9).

text: US federal AI policy is currently defined by two Trump administration executive orders: EO 14179 ('Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence,' signed January 23, 2025) and EO 14365 ('Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence,' signed December 11, 2025); neither is a law passed by Congress and neither directly regulates what an AI company must do.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Federal Register: 'Executive Order 14365 of December 11, 2025 Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence'; 'Executive Order 14179 of January 23, 2025 Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence'. Both direct agencies only.
notes: Other AI orders exist (14318-14320 July 2025, 14409 June 2026), so 'defined by two' is a simplification.

text: The Biden 2023 Executive Order on Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI defined AI broadly as a machine-based system making predictions, recommendations or decisions based on human-defined objectives.
label: correct
evidence_quote: EO 14110 Sec 3(b): 'a machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-defined objectives, make predictions, recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments.'

text: The Biden AI Executive Order paid special attention to 'dual-use foundation models' exhibiting or capable of being modified to exhibit high levels of performance, analogous to the AI Act's treatment of 'very capable foundation models'.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: EO 14110 Sec 3(k): ''dual-use foundation model'' means an AI model ... that exhibits, or could be easily modified to exhibit, high levels of performance at tasks that pose a serious risk to security'
notes: EO part right. The AI Act (2024 and consolidated text) contains neither 'very capable' nor 'foundation model'; that term came from 2023 negotiation drafts.

text: The Biden Executive Order primarily outlined guidelines for federal agencies to shape industry practice and did not impose direct regulation on private entities except for reporting requirements invoked via the Defense Production Act, unlike the EU AI Act which directly applies to any GPAI provider operating within the EU.
label: correct
evidence_quote: EO 14110 Sec 4.2(a): 'in accordance with the Defense Production Act ... the Secretary of Commerce shall require: (i) Companies developing or demonstrating an intent to develop potential dual-use foundation models to provide the Federal Government ... with information, reports, or records'
notes: The EO also used IEEPA for rules on cloud (IaaS) providers, Sec 4.2(c)-(e), which the claim leaves out.

text: The July 2025 US AI Action Plan aims to massively boost US data center capacity and cloud services, and includes an Executive Order promoting export of American AI technology.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Plan: 'Create Streamlined Permitting for Data Centers ...'; 'The United States must meet global demand for AI by exporting its full AI technology stack'; EO 14320 'Promoting the Export of the American AI Technology Stack' (July 23, 2025)
notes: The export order was signed the same day, separately from the plan document.

text: EU AI policies are significantly more cautious than current US federal-level AI policy, though several US states maintain more cautious laws absent a federal mandate.
label: unverifiable
notes: Pure interpretation.

text: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework is a voluntary US framework organized around four core functions: Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage, in contrast to the EU AI Act's binding legal obligations.
label: correct
evidence_quote: NIST AI 100-1: 'four specific functions ... GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE'; 'The Framework is intended to be voluntary'

text: NIST AI RMF describes voluntary risk-management activity, whereas the EU AI Act imposes binding product duties on providers and deployers plus enforcement mechanisms.
label: correct
evidence_quote: 'The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is intended for voluntary use'

text: Organizations operating in both the US and EU markets typically use NIST AI RMF as an internal operating model to help produce evidence supporting EU AI Act compliance, without it substituting for legal compliance.
label: unverifiable
notes: About company practice.

text: The AI Act and the Biden Executive Order/Stanford proposals all use closely aligned definitions of 'foundation model'/'general-purpose AI model', tracing to Bommasani et al. (2021), though the AI Act distinguishes models 'with systemic risk' while the Stanford proposal and US framing refer to 'high-impact' or 'dual-use' models.
label: unverifiable
notes: Main point is an interpretation (definitions aligned, academic origin).

text: For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (e.g., biometrics), where harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied, the provider may choose between internal control conformity assessment (Annex VI, involving the provider's own quality management system) or third-party assessment involving a notified body based on assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation (Annex VII).
supporting_types: eu_guidance | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 43(1): 'the provider shall opt for one of the following conformity assessment procedures based on: (a) the internal control referred to in Annex VI; or (b) the assessment of the quality management system and the assessment of the technical documentation, with the involvement of a notified body, referred to in Annex VII.' Annex VI point 2: 'The provider verifies that the established quality management system is in compliance with the requirements of Article 17.'

text: For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products, or are themselves products, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, Section A, the provider must follow the conformity assessment procedure required under that sectoral legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with the AI Act's specific requirements.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 43(3): 'the provider of the system shall follow the relevant conformity assessment procedure as required in accordance with the relevant Union harmonisation legislation. The requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter shall apply to those high-risk AI systems and shall be part of that assessment.'

text: Annex VII conformity assessment (notified body route) is treated by industry sources as mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI, while most other high-risk AI systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Art 43(2): 'For high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III, providers shall follow the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control as referred to in Annex VI, which does not provide for the involvement of a notified body.'
notes: Critical infrastructure is Annex III point 2, which uses internal control; biometrics may also use Annex VI when standards are applied (Art 43(1)).

text: Under Article 43, for the conformity assessment procedure referred to in Annex VII, the provider may choose any notified body, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority shall act as the notified body.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 43(1): 'the provider may choose any of the notified bodies. However, where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions ... the market surveillance authority ... shall act as a notified body.'

text: A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 43(4): 'shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification' ... changes 'pre-determined by the provider at the moment of the initial conformity assessment ... shall not constitute a substantial modification.'

text: Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, to authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for exceptional reasons of public security, life/health protection, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, for a limited period.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 46(1): 'By way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, any market surveillance authority may authorise ... for exceptional reasons of public security or the protection of life and health of persons, environmental protection or the protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets.'

text: Annex VII, point 4.5, provides that where necessary to assess conformity with Chapter III, Section 2 requirements, and after all other reasonable means have been exhausted, a notified body may be granted access (upon reasoned request) to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, subject to existing Union IP law.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Annex VII 4.5: 'after all other reasonable means to verify conformity have been exhausted and have proven to be insufficient, and upon a reasoned request, the notified body shall also be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including its relevant parameters.'

text: Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts (per Article 97) to update Annex VI (internal control procedure) and Annex VII (QMS and technical documentation assessment) in light of technical progress.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 43(5): 'The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend Annexes VI and VII by updating them in light of technical progress.'

text: Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 35 heading: 'Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies'

text: A Council document sets out an annex (Annex I.A codes, e.g., AIP 0101–0105) defining categories/scope of AI systems subject to Annex I of the AI Act for the designation of conformity assessment (notified) bodies under Article 30 of the Regulation.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Council doc 7322/26: '1. AI systems subject to Annex I of the AI Act AIA Code AIP 0101 AI systems subject to Annex I.A.1. of the AI Act. ... AIP 0105 AI systems subject to Annex I.A.5. of the AI Act.'
notes: The final Annex XIV starts at AIP 0102, but the claim is about the Council document.

text: A proposed COM(2025) 836 regulation would create a new Annex XIV for the Commission's NANDO information system listing codes and corresponding AI system types, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements into aviation safety rules.
label: correct
evidence_quote: 'a new Annex XIV for the Commission's New Approach Notified and Designated Organisations ('NANDO') information system'; 'Article 2 makes amendments with regards to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139'

text: As of March 2026, no AI Act-specific notified bodies had yet been designated; designation processes were described as still ongoing across member states, with limited capacity and uncertain timelines ahead of the August 2026 high-risk obligation deadline.
label: correct
evidence_quote: NANDO search, legislation 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on artificial intelligence', checked 4 Oct 2026: 0 results for Active, Withdrawn and Suspended.
notes: Descriptive parts set aside; in March 2026 the deadline was still August 2026.

text: As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical device AI systems.
label: correct
evidence_quote: NANDO search, legislation 'Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on artificial intelligence', checked 4 Oct 2026: 0 results for Active, Withdrawn and Suspended.
notes: No AI Act body has ever been listed, so none in April 2026.

text: High-risk AI obligations (including conformity assessment requirements) are described as fully applying from August 2, 2026 / August 2026, making this the key compliance deadline, with notified body designation under the AI Act expected only post-2026.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Art 113(c) as amended: 'Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'
notes: Endorses 2 Aug 2026 as the key deadline (unlike C107); the 'expected' part is unverifiable.

text: As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 designated under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR), but these are MDR/IVDR designations, not AI Act designations.
label: correct
evidence_quote: SWD(2025) 1051: 'as of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated bodies'

text: For comparison, under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), whose notified body rules started applying 11 June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated in the Commission's NANDO database as of late June 2026; Article 35(2) of the CRA sets a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity, with full application from 11 December 2027.
label: correct
evidence_quote: CRA Art 71(2): 'Chapter IV (Articles 35 to 51) shall apply from 11 June 2026'; Art 35(2): 'Member States shall strive to ensure, by 11 December 2026 that there is a sufficient number of notified bodies'; applies 'from 11 December 2027'. NANDO, CRA, Active, 4 Oct 2026: 0 results.

text: The Commission publishes lists of designated notified bodies (for various EU legislation, including medical devices) in the NANDO information system, which can be filtered by legislation.
label: correct
evidence_quote: NANDO free search has a 'Legislation' filter; AI Act Art 35(2): 'The Commission shall make publicly available the list of the bodies notified under this Regulation'

text: Under the 2021 Commission proposal text of Article 43, for high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III where harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, the provider was to opt for one of the listed conformity assessment procedures.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 43(1) (2021 proposal): 'the provider shall follow one of the following procedures'

text: Under the original AI Act as adopted in 2024, obligations for high-risk AI systems, including those in Annex III, were to become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e., 2 August 2026.
supporting_types: eu_guidance | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog | legal_analysis
label: incorrect

notes: Annex III applied 24 months after entry into force; 36 months is the Art 6(1) date, 2 Aug 2027. The 'error inside a claim' from the earlier blog post.

text: The amending Regulation is identified as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
label: correct
evidence_quote: Title: 'REGULATION (EU) 2026/1744 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689 ...'

evidence_quote: Art 113(c) as amended: 'Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'

text: Under Article 111(2)/Article 113 transitional provisions, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems (other than certain excepted systems) that were placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (2 August 2026 per one source), only if those systems undergo significant design changes from that date.
label: incorrect
evidence_quote: Art 111(2) as amended: systems placed 'before the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113'

text: High-risk AI systems that are safety components of products regulated under EU product safety law and listed via Annex I will have obligations applying from 2 August 2028 under the amended timeline.
supporting_types: eu_guidance | eu_guidance | eu_guidance | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog | news_blog
label: correct
evidence_quote: Art 113(c) as amended: 'Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), shall apply from: (i) 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III; and (ii) 2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'
